primitives.name: Contrastive Visual-Textual Embedding
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - **Dual encoders + contrastive loss**: image encoder (ResNet-50/101, RN50x4/x16/x64; ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, ViT-L/14, ViT-L/14@336px) and text encoder (Transformer) → linear projection to a shared embedding space.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'f_{\\text{img}}': 'image embedding vector, dimension d', 'f_{\\text{text}}': 'text embedding vector, dimension d', 'sim(\\cdot, \\cdot)': 'cosine similarity, unitless', 'τ': 'learnable temperature scalar, unitless'}
primitives.assumptions: Embeddings are learned in a shared space such that semantically similar image-text pairs are closer than dissimilar ones; contrastive loss ensures global alignment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When semantic ambiguity arises (e.g., 'boxer' as dog vs. athlete), performance degrades due to lack of explicit disambiguation in pretraining.

layer2.mapping: CLIP's dual encoder maps visual and textual inputs into a common semantic space; GSE uses this for zero-shot classification of play concepts by querying with natural language.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of zero-shot classification on unseen sports concepts.

primitives.name: Zero-Shot Classifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Zero-shot transfer**: encode class names (or descriptions) with the text encoder → cosine-similarity classifier with L2-normalized inputs/weights, no bias, temperature scaling.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p(c|x)': 'probability of class c given image x, unitless', 'f_{\\text{img}}': 'image embedding vector, dimension d', 'f_{\\text{text}}^c': 'text embedding for class c, dimension d', 'τ': 'temperature scalar, unitless'}
primitives.assumptions: Class names carry sufficient semantic information to distinguish concepts; zero-shot generalization holds across domains.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when class labels are ambiguous or lack descriptive richness (e.g., "crane" or "boxer").

layer2.mapping: The zero-shot classifier is derived from CLIP's embedding space; GSI applies it to infer posterior distributions over game states using natural language prompts.
layer2.telemetry: Top-k accuracy on unseen sports categories.

primitives.name: Prompt Ensemble
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Prompt engineering + ensembling**: default template "A photo of a {label}." (+1.3% ImageNet); task-specific templates (e.g., "a type of pet", quoted OCR text, "a satellite photo of..."); ensemble over 80 prompt variants on ImageNet (+3.5%), averaged in EMBEDDING space (cost = single classifier when amortized).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'K': 'number of prompt variants, dimensionless', 'f_{\\text{text}}^{c,k}': 'text embedding for class c under prompt k, dimension d', 'p(c|x)': 'ensemble probability of class c given image x, unitless'}
primitives.assumptions: Ensemble of prompts improves robustness to linguistic variation; each prompt variant contributes independently to classification.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Performance degrades if prompts do not adequately represent domain-specific semantics (e.g., football terminology).

layer2.mapping: Prompt ensembling enhances CLIP’s zero-shot capability by aggregating multiple linguistic interpretations; GSE uses this to improve retrieval of complex play concepts.
layer2.telemetry: Mean average precision (mAP) over retrieved play concepts.

reasoning_traces.think:
CLIP's core innovation lies in its dual-encoder architecture trained via contrastive learning on massive web-scale image-text pairs. The model learns to map both images and text into a shared embedding space where semantic similarity is captured via cosine distance. This enables zero-shot transfer by treating class labels as text prompts and computing similarity scores between image embeddings and prompt embeddings. The symmetric cross-entropy loss (InfoNCE) encourages correct pairings while penalizing incorrect ones. The key mathematical structure is a similarity matrix S ∈ R^{N×N}, where N is the batch size, and the loss function maximizes log-likelihood of true pairs. The learnable temperature τ scales logits to prevent numerical instability. Prompt engineering enhances performance by varying how classes are described, leading to ensembled embeddings that better generalize. In GSI, these embeddings support Bayesian inference over game states, while in GSE, they enable real-time classification and retrieval of play concepts.
